Q: Printing to a remote printer from a website A:

🚨 IMPORTANT TRUTH (NO WORKAROUND INSIDE DOCKER)

You are running inside Docker (Linux):

/var/www/html/app/...

But your Star TSP100III printer is on Windows 11 Pro (local USB / shared).

👉 A Linux Docker container CANNOT print directly to a Windows local printer.
👉 Browser location does NOT matter.
👉 print, copy, cmd, Windows spooler do not exist in Docker.

This is not a code problem anymore.

❌ WHY IT WILL NEVER WORK THIS WAY

What you tryWhy it failsprint /D:Windows-onlycmd /cWindows-onlycopy \\localhost\PrinterWindows-onlyESC/POSDriver blocks itDocker → Windows printer❌ Impossible

Docker runs on Linux kernel, isolated from Windows devices.

✅ WHAT WILL WORK (REAL SOLUTIONS)

You have ONLY 3 VALID OPTIONS.
Anything else is a dead end.

🟢 OPTION 1 (BEST & CORRECT – RECOMMENDED)

🔹 Print from the CLIENT PC (Browser Side)

This is how POS systems actually work.

Flow:

Browser → JavaScript → Local printer

How:

  • Use Star WebPRNT

  • Or Star CloudPRNT

  • Or Electron / Local helper app

✔ Works from anywhere
✔ No server printing
✔ No Docker issues
✔ Official Star solution

👉 THIS IS THE INDUSTRY STANDARD

🟢 OPTION 2 (WINDOWS PRINT SERVICE – MIDDLEWARE)

Create a small Windows service that listens for print jobs.

Flow:

Docker (PHP) → HTTP API → Windows Print Service → Printer

Example:

  • PHP sends JSON receipt

  • Windows service prints it

✔ Works reliably
✔ Full printer control
❌ Requires extra service

🟡 OPTION 3 (LINUX SERVER + USB PRINTER)

Only works if:

  • Printer is connected to Linux host

  • CUPS installed

  • RAW printing enabled

❌ Not your setup
❌ Star Windows driver not usable

🚫 WHAT YOU MUST STOP TRYING

❌ Printing from Docker to Windows printer
❌ Using print, cmd, copy
❌ Expecting ESC/POS to work
❌ Server-side printing for POS

This cannot be fixed with PHP.

✅ THE CORRECT SOLUTION

Since:

  • You are building a POS

  • Printing happens at the counter

  • Printer is local to cashier PC

  • App is web-based

👉 You MUST use CLIENT-SIDE PRINTING

⭐ RECOMMENDED: STAR WebPRNT

Official Star solution for browsers.

What it gives you:

✔ Print from Chrome / Edge
✔ Auto-cut
✔ Logo
✔ Barcode / QR
✔ Cash drawer
✔ Works with TSP100III

Q: How to retrieve all paths of a source node without a target node using networkx A:

I am not that familiar with networkx packages but it could be done via igraph like below.

For efficiency, you can take the divide-and-conquer strategy to find all simple paths if the graphs consists of multiple connected components. For example

# !pip install python-igraph

import igraph as ig

# create graph as example shows
G = ig.Graph(directed=True)
node_names = [str(i) for i in range(1, 11)]
G.add_vertices(node_names)

edges = [("1", "2"), ("1", "6"), ("2", "3"), ("2", "5"), ("3", "4"), ("6", "9"), ("7", "8"), ("8", "9")]
G.add_edges(edges)

# decompose graph into subgraphs and find all simple paths per subgraph
subG = G.decompose(mode = "weak")
all_simple_paths = []
for g in subG:
  src = [idx for idx in g.vs if g.degree(idx, mode = 'in') == 0]
  des = [idx for idx in g.vs if g.degree(idx, mode = 'out') == 0]
  for s in src:
    ps = g.get_all_simple_paths(s, des)
    for p in ps:
      all_simple_paths.append([v['name'] for v in g.vs if v.index in p])

and print(all_simple_paths) will show you

[['1', '2', '3', '4'], ['1', '2', '5'], ['1', '6', '9'], ['7', '8', '9']]

Q: How to make dynamic modal window depending on element id? A:

A crude and simple way to do it would be to make a simple div. Style it the way you want a modal to appear. Adjust z-index accordingly. Set display as none.

When the product is clicked, set the innerHTML of the div with the details you want, and set the display as block.

You can also integrate bootstrap modal, but try to code a basic sample yourself to learn how it works.
